name: DanceSport at Cornell
description: The purpose of Cornell DanceSport is to teach and promote competitive ballroom dancing within the Cornell community. We aim to help each other improve in our dancing by providing space and lessons on campus, and push ourselves to succeed in competition by traveling to intercollegiate competitions throughout the northeast.

name: Data for Good in Policy at Cornell
description: Our mission is to equip Cornell students with data analytics skills for real-world impact through hands-on workshops, consulting projects for public-interest clients, and guest speakers.

name: Data Journal at Cornell
description: Our mission is to provide Cornell undergraduate students the opportunity to explore the fields of data science, data visualization, and data journalism.

name: Data Science Club at Cornell
description: Current initiatives range from devising a scalable mapping system for better natural disaster response to developing a tool that can summarize Amazon reviews for a better user experience. Our team of 70+ students is a great place to meet people with diverse interests, gain experience at the intersection of theory and application, and contribute to the greater community initiatives.

name: Deixa Sambar
description: Deixa Sambar is a musical ensemble comitted to playing, teaching, and sharing various genres of Brazilian music on Cornell's campus and in the greater Ithaca area.

name: Delta Chi
description: Delta Chi was founded as a law fraternity on October 13th, 1890 at Cornell University. In 1922, a collective body of members decided to register Delta Chi as a general fraternity, thereby opening membership to men of any academic discipline. In 1929, Delta Chi became the first fraternity to abolish the hazing practices associated with "hell week." Since that time, Delta Chi has evolved into an international organization, now including 120 chapters and colonies, and over 90,000 members worldwide.

name: Kedma
description: Kedma is the Orthodox organization at Cornell that provides for the religious and social needs of Orthodox Jews. Kedma is dedicated to upholding Orthodox values and maintaining a comfortable atmosphere for Orthodox students. By working with other student organizations, Kedma provides focused, well resourced programs and events for Orthodox students, as well as for the Cornell community at large. Kedma oversees the Orthodox prayer services held three times a day on campus. Kedma also maintains the Eruv at Cornell, which allows Jewish students on campus to carry on the Sabbath.

name: Kehilat Shevach: Cornell's Traditional Egalitarian Community
description: Shevach is Cornell's Traditional-Egalitarian (Conservative) minyan. We provide a community for students seeking a traditional Jewish prayer space that allows for egalitarian participation. We meet for traditional Shabbat services every Friday evening. We also hold periodic Shabbat morning services, programming for major Jewish holidays, and social events.

name: Kendo Club at Cornell University
description: The purpose of the Kendo Club at Cornell University shall be to provide a space and environment for students interested in the Japanese martial art of Kendo, and to practice, compete, and improve together.

name: Key Elements
description: The Key Elements take a cappella to new heights at Cornell University by bringing their unique energy and excitement to every performance. As a co-ed a cappella group, we perform innovative arrangements of songs from the classic rock genre along with other contemporary popular music that cannot be mimicked. We strive to not only provide Cornell with awe-inspiring music and concerts, but to also offer an opportunity for students of any background to pursue their musical passions, while creating lifelong friendships along the way.

name: Khiladi at Cornell
description: The purpose of Khiladi at Cornell shall be to foster cultural expression, creativity, and community through South Asian fusion dance. The organization shall promote diversity and cultural appreciation within the Cornell community and beyond by engaging in performances, competitions, and events that integrate Indian and Western dance styles.

name: Kidney Disease Screening and Awareness Program
description: The Kidney Disease Screening and Awareness Program (KDSAP) is a student-run organization that provides free kidney health screenings and health education to underserved communities. Students are working under the supervision of Adult expertise providing supervision of students who will provide educational materials We provide programs geared towards improving the health of underserved populations.

name: Materials Science and Engineering Graduate Student Association at Cornell
description: The purpose of LATTICE shall be to foster the growth of graduate students by promoting interaction, collaboration, and professional development. Through community-building, education, and advocacy, we aim to cultivate a culture of integrity, excellence, and mutual support that ensures the success of our members and the advancement of materials science research.

name: Materials Society at Cornell
description: The Materials Society at Cornell represents the university's undergraduate chapter of The Materials Research Society (MRS), The Materials Information Society (ASM), The Minerals, Metals, and Materials Society (TMS), and American Ceramics Society (ACerS). We partner with Materials Advantage to bring students to professional organizations (ACeRS, TMS, ASM, and AIST) at an affordable price. CMS is a student-run organization devoted to unity of MS&E majors and others interested in the fields of nanotechnology, biomedical engineering, semiconductors, polymers, ceramics, glasses, and metals.

name: Med-In Black Association
description: We, the aspiring Black pre-health students, in our pursuit of academic excellence and a future in healthcare, do hereby establish the Black Pre-Health Alliance. In recognition of our shared aspirations, unique experiences, and the challenges we face on our journey toward careers in health and medicine, we unite under this banner to forge a community of support, empowerment, and advocacy. We acknowledge the historic underrepresentation of Black individuals across health professions and the urgent need to address disparities in healthcare. name: Media & Entertainment at Cornell
description: To educate students who are interested in media about professional skills. To facilitate intercultural communication through hosting entertainment events.

name: Media Guild, Inc
description: The Cornell Media Guild, Inc. provides students with the opportunity to gain comprehensive media training/experience based on the operation of WVBR 93.5 FM, CornellRadio.net, and Electric Buffalo Records.

name: Sloan Student Association
description: The Sloan Student Association facilitates networking opportunities with prospective employers, professional development programs, community service involvement, and formal and informal social activities. Our activities center around the goals of furthering our “Sloan Family” and addressing MHA students’ needs.

name: Slope Media Group
description: As Cornell's multimedia powerhouse, Slope Media Group is a leader in Cornell-related media and entertainment, delivering a creative, student perspective on everything that matters to the Big Red community. Slope is for students, by students.

name: Smith Family Business Initiative
description: The Smith Family Business Initiative at Cornell is dedicated to supporting and strengthening the network of businesses that are family and privately owned.

name: Snail Mail Club at Cornell
description: The purpose of Snail Mail Club at Cornell shall be to create an environment and provide the supplies for traditional postal mail, centralized as an expression of creativity, care and friendship.

name: Snee Graduate Organization
description: The mission of the Snee Graduate Organization is to enhance the professional and social interaction between graduate students in the fields of Geological and Atmospheric Sciences. The organization also serves as a medium for communication between the graduate student body and the faculty of the Earth and Atmospheric Sciences at Cornell University.

name: Snodgrass and Wigglesworth - Cornell Undergraduate Entomology Club
description: The purpose of Snodgrass and Wigglesworth shall be to, in affiliation with the Cornell Department of Entomology, promote the study and appreciation of arthropods. The goals of Snodgrass and Wigglesworth are: 1. To foster a cohesive community among the Cornell undergraduates interested in arthropods, with a focus on insects. 2. To spread awareness and appreciation of entomology throughout the Cornell campus and Ithaca area. 3.
